title: Naturality of block projections of active concatenation
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], symmetric infinity-operads, their inert edges and active and inert pointed maps of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], and the active concatenation $\oplus$ of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation]. Let $\mathcal C^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ be a symmetric infinity-operad, let $s\geq0$, and let $F:(\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})^s\to\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ be the $s$-fold ordered concatenation $\mathbf x=(x_1,\ldots,x_s)\mapsto\bigoplus_{j=1}^sx_j$, the empty tuple when $s=0$. Write $\iota:\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}\to\mathcal C^\otimes$ for the inclusion and $\mathrm{pr}_j$ for the $j$th projection of the product. If $x_j$ lies over $\langle r_j\rangle$ and $r=\sum_jr_j$, then $F(\mathbf x)$ lies over $\langle r\rangle$, and for an active tuple $\mathbf h=(h_j:x_j\to x_j')$ with pointed maps $\gamma_j$ the arrow $F(\mathbf h)$ lies over the blockwise sum $\coprod_j\gamma_j$, which sends the $j$th consecutive input block into the $j$th output block. For each $j$ there is a coherent transformation $p_j:\iota F\Rightarrow\iota\,\mathrm{pr}_j$ of functors $(\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})^s\to\mathcal C^\otimes$, whose component $p_j(\mathbf x):F(\mathbf x)\to x_j$ is an inert edge over the block projection $q_j:\langle r\rangle\to\langle r_j\rangle$ (the identity of the $j$th block onto $\langle r_j\rangle$, every other input to the basepoint). In particular, for every active tuple $\mathbf h:\mathbf x\to\mathbf x'$ there are coherent squares $p_j(\mathbf x')\,F(\mathbf h)\simeq h_j\,p_j(\mathbf x)$, with all higher simplices of these naturality data. Empty blocks $r_j=0$ are included; for $s=1$ the transformation $p_1$ is an equivalence $F\simeq\mathrm{id}$, and for $s=0$ there are no projections.

proof.text: Put $S=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and $p:\mathcal C^\otimes\to S$. Apply [lem-coef-active-operad-envelope-cocartesian] to $p$, with $S$ the commutative operad. Its extra equivalence-lifting hypothesis holds: an equivalence in $S$ is a permutation and hence inert, so it has an operadic cocartesian lift. This lift is an equivalence: in the homotopy-pullback mapping square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], precomposition on the bottom is an equivalence, so precomposition on the top is an equivalence for every target. Taking the source as target gives a left inverse; injectivity on components with the original target then gives the right inverse. The inverse-component criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] makes this an equivalence edge. Thus the envelope $H=\mathcal C^\otimes\times_S\operatorname{Act}(S)$ has a cocartesian projection $r:H\to S$, is itself an infinity-operad, and an $r$-cocartesian edge has inert source edge under $u:H\to\mathcal C^\otimes$.

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1, Corollary 2.2.4.5 and Remark 2.2.4.6; explicit envelope calculation (agent proof, archive WANTED).

proof.text: The fiber $H_{\langle1\rangle}$ identifies with $\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$. An object is $(x,\mu_n)$, where $x$ lies over $\langle n\rangle$ and $\mu_n$ is the unique active fold. An arrow has source pointed map $\gamma:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$ satisfying $\mu_m\gamma=\mu_n$, precisely the condition that $\gamma$ is active. The same description of a simplex as a chain in the ordinary base gives the identification in every degree. The operadic Segal equivalence of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction] for $H$, whose inert edges are supplied by the envelope theorem, identifies $H_{\langle s\rangle}$ with $(H_{\langle1\rangle})^s$. By [lem-coef-symmetric-monoidal-segal-classification], this is the symmetric monoidal envelope and transport along $\mu_s$ computes its $s$-ary tensor, hence the active concatenation of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation].

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1, Corollary 2.2.4.5 and Remark 2.2.4.6; explicit envelope calculation (agent proof, archive WANTED).

proof.text: Let $K=(\mathcal C^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})^s$, enlarging the ambient universe so it is small. Choose a coherent quasi-inverse $A:K\to H_{\langle s\rangle}$ to the Segal equivalence of step 2, together with its comparison to the identity on $K$. For each $j$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] to $r:H\to S$, the diagram $A$ (viewed in $H$), and the constant base transformation $\rho_j:\langle s\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$. This produces a coherent transformation $L_j:A\Rightarrow D_j$ with cocartesian components. Here $D_j:K\to H_{\langle1\rangle}$ is the $j$th inert transport; choose the transports used in the Segal comparison, so that comparison supplies a coherent equivalence $D_j\simeq\mathrm{pr}_j$. Applying the simplicial functor $u$ yields a transformation $uA\Rightarrow uD_j$ with inert components, by the envelope edge criterion. Postcomposing with the displayed equivalence gives a coherent transformation $uA\Rightarrow\iota\mathrm{pr}_j$. Composition with this equivalence preserves inertness by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], since equivalences in a fixed operadic fiber are cocartesian over its identity (the mapping criterion).

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1, Corollary 2.2.4.5 and Remark 2.2.4.6; explicit envelope calculation (agent proof, archive WANTED).

proof.text: Here is the finite-set calculation identifying the source diagram and its projections. Write $A(\mathbf x)=(z,a:\langle r\rangle\to\langle s\rangle)$. Its $j$th inert transport has underlying source edge selecting exactly $a^{-1}(j)$: in the envelope square the other map is the active fold on that subset. Thus its color tuple is $x_j$ by the Segal comparison. Label the inputs of $z$ by the consecutive ordered blocks of these color tuples. This is the ordered concatenation convention; it can be imposed on the whole diagram by applying the corresponding permutations, with the permutation comparisons retained. The square over $\mu_s$ with source edge $1_z$ and target object $(z,\mu_r)$ is envelope-cocartesian, since $1_z$ is inert. It is defined on every simplex of $A$ simply by composing its active arrow $a$ with $\mu_s$. Consequently $uA$ is the envelope model of the functor $\iota F$ in step 2, coherently with its chosen tensor comparison. The source edge of $L_j$ lies over $q_j$, the projection retaining the $j$th block. An arrow of $A$ has pointed map $\gamma$ satisfying $a'\gamma=a$; thus it preserves the block index, and its restriction on block $j$ is the pointed map $\gamma_j$ of $h_j$. Hence the source pointed map of $F(\mathbf h)$ is exactly $\coprod_j\gamma_j$. Under the coherent tensor comparison, the transformations of step 3 are the required $p_j$.

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1, Corollary 2.2.4.5 and Remark 2.2.4.6; explicit envelope calculation (agent proof, archive WANTED).

proof.text: The transformation obtained in step 3 is a simplicial map $K\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C^\otimes$, not a choice of separate objectwise edges. Restriction along an edge $\mathbf h$ of $K$ gives the square $p_j(\mathbf x')F(\mathbf h)\simeq h_jp_j(\mathbf x)$. Restriction along every higher simplex gives its higher naturality data; all faces and degeneracies commute because they are restrictions of that same map. This proves the asserted coherence directly from the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Construction 2.2.4.1, Corollary 2.2.4.5 and Remark 2.2.4.6; explicit envelope calculation (agent proof, archive WANTED).

proof.text: If $r_j=0$, its block is empty and $q_j$ is still inert: it has no non-basepoint outputs to test. The operadic zero fiber is terminal-equivalent, so the Segal and transport constructions above still apply. For $s=0$, the tensor is the empty tuple by [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation], the sum of arities is zero, and there is no index $j$. For $s=1$, the envelope Segal comparison is unary and $q_1$ is the identity. Every component of $p_1$ is therefore cocartesian over an identity, hence an equivalence by the mapping-square inverse argument of step 1. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] to conclude that $p_1:F\simeq\mathrm{id}$ is a coherent equivalence.
